analysis.title: Refocus equity exposure
key_insights: UBS CIO moved global equities to Neutral but still expects markets to rise, with end-2027 price targets of 8,200 for the S&P 500, 7,000 for the Euro Stoxx 50, 1,170 for MSCI Asia ex-Japan and 1,460 for MSCI AC World.
UBS expects resilient economic activity and continued AI investment to support corporate profits and further equity gains in 2027.
Earnings growth forecasts for 2027 are around 15% for both the US and Eurozone and 20% for Asia ex-Japan.
UBS expects AI investment to rise from around USD 1.0tr in 2026 to USD 1.4tr in 2027. Differences in companies' ability to monetize AI should lead to greater earnings dispersion.
The 10 largest companies make up around 40% of the S&P 500, so revisions to a small group of earnings forecasts have an outsized effect on index returns.
The Eurozone is the preferred regional equity market: 15% earnings growth in 2027, matching the US, from a lower starting valuation and with less dependence on concentrated AI-linked companies.

Supports for Eurozone profits: global revenues of listed European companies, recovering manufacturing, and investment in defense, infrastructure, automation and electrification. Healthier banks and relatively low private sector debt add to the case.

US equities moved to Neutral after a period of exceptional earnings growth and a strong market advance. Markets are focusing on whether the investment cycle can support profits into 2028. Cannibalization, financing and execution risks around AI have increased.

Asia ex-Japan and emerging market equities moved to Neutral because their opportunity sets are heavily weighted toward semiconductors, memory and technology hardware, which leaves earnings and valuations exposed to the AI capital-spending cycle.
Within Asia, UBS favors financials in China, Japan and Singapore, China health care, and domestic-demand beneficiaries in India, Japan and Singapore.

UBS favors industrials and health care to broaden earnings exposure beyond technology. In industrials it prefers companies serving several end markets with visible orders over those heavily dependent on data center construction.
Investors should keep strategic US exposure but use market strength to reduce excess concentration, for example through equal-weight strategies, and should focus on financially strong tech companies.

sector_views.rationale: Automation, defense, transport infrastructure, power networks and electrification investment should support earnings. UBS prefers multi-end-market companies with visible orders over those dependent on data center construction.
Medical innovation, obesity treatments, diagnostics and medical technology support revenues, and earnings are less tied to corporate investment.
UBS says to focus on financially strong tech companies and reduce excess concentration. Earnings dispersion is expected to rise as companies differ in their ability to monetize AI.
Favored for income, rate normalization and balance sheet strength.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts 2027 earnings growth of around 15% for the US, around 15% for the Eurozone and 20% for Asia ex-Japan. These are UBS forecasts, not reported figures.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce excess US megacap concentration and use equal-weight strategies while retaining strategic US exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: High index concentration and high earnings expectations raise sensitivity to disappointment from a few companies.

trade_ideas.description: Favor Eurozone equities, industrials and health care to diversify across regions and earnings drivers
trade_ideas.rationale: Eurozone earnings growth of 15% in 2027 from a lower starting valuation, with less dependence on AI-linked companies.

risk_factors: High earnings expectations and elevated US market concentration leave indices more sensitive to disappointment from a small number of companies.
Cannibalization, financing and execution risks around AI have increased.
A further rise in discount rates.
Uncertainty over whether the current investment cycle can support profits into 2028.
Asia ex-Japan and EM earnings and valuations are exposed to the AI capital-spending cycle through semiconductors, memory and technology hardware.
vol_and_positioning: The 10 largest companies are around 40% of the S&P 500, so index returns are unusually sensitive to earnings revisions at a small group of companies.
UBS says the path to further gains could be volatile, and the market is more sensitive to earnings disappointment or a further rise in discount rates.

tension_points.theme: US equity concentration and AI earnings
tension_points.bull_case: Resilient activity and AI investment rising to USD 1.4tr in 2027 support about 15% US earnings growth and further equity gains, with an S&P 500 target of 8,200.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointment in earnings at a small number of large companies, or a further rise in discount rates.
